notes.title: Small function objects with lambdas and explicit context
notes.core: Use lambdas for short behaviors assigned to a single-abstract-method interface, preserving readable target types and concise business rules. Prefer a named method or class when logic becomes complex, requires independent object identity, or needs a non-functional base type.
rules: A lambda requires a target functional interface; it cannot directly instantiate an abstract class or a multi-abstract-method interface.
Keep generic parameterization at the API boundary so lambda parameter and result types can be inferred safely.
A lambda’s this is lexically bound to its enclosing instance, whereas an anonymous class has its own this.
Captured local variables must be final or effectively final; this does not make captured mutable objects thread-safe.
Use a named method or constant-specific class body when enum behavior needs complex logic or instance state unavailable during enum constant construction.
Do not use serialized lambda implementation details as a stable cross-version wire format.
nuance: A functional interface can contain default/static methods without losing its single abstract method property.
A short lambda can be less clear than a named method if business intent is hidden in nested expressions.
Java 21 records, switch expressions and pattern matching can simplify code inside a lambda, but do not remove target typing or capture rules.
An anonymous class remains useful for abstract classes, interfaces with multiple abstract methods, or code that needs the function object itself.
notes.misconception: A lambda is merely a shorter anonymous class with identical this, inheritance and serialization semantics.
notes.production_context: A retry-policy router stores concise predicate rules and uses named policy objects when rule evaluation requires diagnostics or mutable lifecycle.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 adds modern syntax inside lambdas but retains Java 8-era target typing, lexical this, effectively-final capture and functional-interface restrictions.
notes.note_scope: Source-informed original item-level draft, not independent paragraph-level semantic review.

notes.title: Method references as readable adapters, not a blanket replacement
notes.core: Use a method reference when it exposes a named operation more clearly than a lambda. Distinguish static, bound instance, unbound instance, class-constructor and array-constructor references, and rely on the functional target signature to determine invocation arguments.
rules: Choose a method reference when the method name explains the behavior better than redundant lambda parameters.
Keep a lambda when parameter names document intent or a reference would obscure the receiver and arguments.
A bound instance reference captures a particular receiver; an unbound instance reference receives its receiver as a functional argument.
Constructor and array-constructor references act as factories with target-compatible signatures.
Check overload resolution, null receivers and target types rather than assuming syntactic brevity guarantees correctness.
Extract complex lambda bodies into a named method before considering a method reference.
nuance: Static method references can often replace pure arithmetic or parsing lambdas, but not arbitrary reordered arguments without an adapter.
A bound method reference evaluates its receiver expression when the reference is created; a lambda can defer receiver evaluation.
Method references and lambdas can have different clarity even when their runtime behavior is equivalent.
Java 21 method-reference target typing remains sensitive to overloaded method signatures and generic inference.
notes.misconception: Method references are always shorter, safer and semantically identical to every visually similar lambda.
notes.production_context: A reconciliation pipeline parses external codes, constructs typed events and merges counters using named conversion functions.
notes.java21_delta: Java 21 retains the five reference forms and target typing described in Java 8-era APIs; new language syntax does not eliminate overload/receiver subtleties.
